tour.title: A connected terminal
tour.copy: Rail receipt, product storage and road dispatch form the main site workflow. Explore how the proposed facilities sit alongside the existing administration block.

tour.title: Receive by railway
tour.copy: The unloading shed is replaced in this view by inverted-L fall-arrester supports at 12.42 m centres. Their dimensions follow the supplied detail; two rows of 27 interpret its 54 places. The original held shed schedule remains in the facility notes.

tour.title: Store by product
tour.copy: Seven above-ground product tanks provide a scheduled 22,200 m³ of product storage. This excludes fire water and the underground vessels.

tour.title: Load and dispatch
tour.copy: Four active lanes have illustrative tankers, loading assemblies and an operator walkway. Four further lanes are marked as future reservations. The 12 × 52 m footprint follows the drawing; structural details and heights are illustrative.

tour.title: Support the operation
tour.copy: Two scheduled fire-water tanks provide 7,300 m³ in total. Power, water treatment, maintenance and administration complete the site.

tour.title: Leave room to grow
tour.copy: The western areas are reserved for future development. They remain open in this model; no future capacity has been invented.

notes.heading: Source of truth
notes.text: The supplied PDF is a raster drawing. The title block identifies KE-8S04B-PI-PPL-0001, Rev D2, dated 24-08-2026, with the issue reason PESO approval for construction. A separate DWG filename says Rev C1. The DWG was not parsed; the model follows the visible PDF revision. The drawing text does not independently verify approval or compliance status.

notes.heading: What is transcribed
notes.text: Tank diameters, shell heights, scheduled stored capacities, roof-type codes, facility names and scheduled footprints come from the PDF. IFRVT denotes an internal floating-roof vertical tank; CRVT denotes a cone-roof vertical tank. Roof details here are illustrative.

notes.heading: What is approximate
notes.text: All positions, the boundary, roads, rail lines, landscape and pipe corridors are manually traced. Scale is calibrated against a 24 m HSD tank. This is not a DWG conversion, survey model, BIM model or construction model. Roads, wall heights, roofs, fittings, pumps, vehicles and most building heights are illustrative. Shown pipes are schematic corridors, not design routing.

notes.heading: Drawing discrepancies and holds
notes.text: The facility schedule gives the unloading shed as 350 × 10 m; a hold note gives its superstructure as 380 × 15 m. The model uses the scheduled size and discloses the hold. Inspection-platform construction is also on hold. Mast quantities/locations require confirmation during detail engineering. The source fire-water capacity does not equal a full cylinder at the listed shell dimensions; listed stored capacity is preserved rather than recalculated.

notes.heading: Ground and direction
notes.text: The drawing states a site reduced level of 19.000 m. This viewer uses flat local grade at Y = 0; it does not model surveyed elevations or drainage. The on-screen compass follows the drawing axis, not true north. Use the full sheet for the original orientation diagram.

notes.heading: Measurements and exports
notes.text: Measurements are horizontal ground-point distances in the approximate trace. They do not test statutory clearances. The GLB export contains visible model geometry in metres with source notes in its metadata. Scene images contain an accuracy caption. Neither export establishes engineering accuracy.

notes.heading: Underground display
notes.text: Five scheduled 3.3 × 7.5 m horizontal underground vessels are shown when Underground is enabled. They are lifted above local grade in the illustrative cutaway for inspection. The small 900-litre sump and minor bore wells, watch towers, potable-water tanks and masts are not individually reconstructed.

notes.heading: Loading gantry visual reference
notes.text: The supplied Fuel and Pol Truck Loading Gantry.png informed common industrial features: steel framing, elevated operator access, handrails, articulated loading arms and flexible hoses. The model is an original procedural design; the reference image is not embedded, reproduced or used as a texture. Four active and four future bays follow the plot-plan schedule. Bay product assignments, loading design, platform height and structural details are illustrative, not engineering specifications.

notes.heading: Publishing and privacy
notes.text: This package includes images derived from your drawing. Publishing to a public repository or GitHub Pages makes them publicly accessible. Confirm the intended audience and permission to share the drawing before publication.

notes.heading: Pump-house visual references
notes.text: The three supplied pump-house photographs inform only the architectural character: open steel columns, roof trusses, green upper cladding, raised pump bases and curved pipework. The model uses independently created geometry and signs. The source footprint and position of each Panchgram pump house are preserved. The photographed crude-unloading label is not applied to this terminal. Modelled pump counts, duty assignments, drivers and routing are illustrative; capacities and engineered configurations are unknown. Photos are excluded from the GitHub-ready ZIP.

notes.heading: Tank-farm visual reference
notes.text: TankStorage-1920x840.jpg informs pale painted shells, restrained seams, roof access railings, external stairs and warm evening lights. Geometry and paint textures are independently generated; the photograph is not embedded and remains excluded from the GitHub ZIP. All nine above-ground tanks preserve scheduled diameters, shell heights, capacities and roof-type tags. Internal floating roof tanks retain closed outer roofs; no exposed floating deck or storage level is inferred from the photograph. Roof slope, foundations, access structures, nozzles, paint and lights are illustrative and are not design or lighting calculations.

notes.heading: Underground vessel visual reference
notes.text: UG Vessel.jpg informs the red-coated horizontal shell, rounded heads, raised access necks and concrete inspection pit. Geometry and signs are original; no reference photograph is embedded. Five vessel diameters of 3.3 m, total end-to-end lengths of 7.5 m and scheduled capacities of 50 m³ each are preserved. Open pit cutaways remove the terrain above the selected inspection display. Soil cover, concrete walls, floor clearances, head shapes, supports, manway counts and nozzle details are illustrative. This represents an inspection view, not an as-built installation or excavation design.
